title: Cats and Other Pets
objective: After this level you can explain why cats were so loved in Egypt.
summary: Cats guarded Egypt’s grain from rodents and snakes, lived as pets and were linked to the goddess Bastet. Greek visitors reported families shaving their eyebrows when a cat died.

cards.headline: Egyptians called a cat “miu.” Say it out loud.
cards.body: The word meant “he or she who mews”: a cat named for its meow. Egyptians loved cats for good practical reasons and good religious ones.

cards.headline: Hired for pest control
cards.body: Cats earned their place. They hunted the rodents that threatened to eat Egypt’s grain and spread disease, and they killed dangerous animals like snakes and scorpions. Pest control was the main reason cats were domesticated at all. A storeroom of Level 4’s wheat and barley needed a guard, and the guard purred. Art shows the rest of the story: cats in collars, lurking under chairs, just like yours.

cards.headline: A goddess with whiskers
cards.body: Cats also had a goddess. Bastet was worshipped first as a lioness and later as a cat, often shown as a woman with a cat’s head. She watched over the home, fertility, joy and the protection of children. Her home city was Bubastis in the Nile Delta, and people wore little cat figures as amulets, probably because of her. From fierce lioness to house cat: Bastet got tamer, just like her animals.

cards.headline: Mourning the family cat
cards.body: Losing a cat hurt. Herodotus, the Greek traveler you met in Level 2, wrote that when a cat died, everyone in the household shaved their eyebrows. For a dog, they shaved their heads and whole bodies. Diodorus, a Greek historian of the 1st century BCE, wrote that he saw an Egyptian crowd kill a Roman who had accidentally killed a cat. These are outsiders’ reports, but they agree: in Egypt, you did not mess with the cat.

questions.prompt: Which Egyptian goddess was worshipped as a lioness and later as a cat?

options.label: Hathor
options.rationale: Hathor is linked to the sistrum, not cats.

options.label: Nut
options.rationale: The lioness who became a cat was Bastet.

questions.explanation: Bastet began as a lioness goddess and was later worshipped as a cat.

questions.prompt: What practical job made cats so valuable to Egyptians?

options.label: Herding sheep in the fields
options.rationale: Cats guarded food; they didn’t herd.

options.label: Guarding houses against thieves
options.rationale: Their enemies were rodents and snakes.

options.label: Carrying messages between villages
options.rationale: That’s not a cat’s job anywhere.

options.label: Hunting rodents that threatened the grain

questions.explanation: Cats hunted rodents that ate grain and spread disease, and killed snakes and scorpions.

questions.prompt: Herodotus, who called Egypt “the gift of the river” in Level 2, also reported what about cats?

options.label: Households shaved their eyebrows when a cat died
Cats were fed only on Nile fish
Cats were trained to guard boats
options.rationale: He described how families mourned a cat.

questions.explanation: He wrote that a household shaved their eyebrows when their cat died a natural death.
